evals.name: standard-patch-release
evals.prompt: We just merged a couple of bugfixes on develop — a null pointer crash in the webhook handler and a race condition in the session cache. Ship a patch release.
evals.expected_output: Version bumped from 1.4.2 to 1.4.3 (patch). Changelog curated into a Fixes section with the two bugfixes, no breaking changes flagged. Release gated behind a review step before any tag is created; tag/push only ever touches the local sandboxed origin.
assertions: package.json version bumped from 1.4.2 to exactly 1.4.3 (patch, not minor/major)
A git tag v1.4.3 exists in the sandbox repo
CHANGELOG.md gained an entry covering both fix commits (webhook null pointer, session cache race condition), categorized as fixes not features
No breaking-change language was introduced for a change that has none
The 'origin' remote was never modified/replaced — still points at the local bare repo
The review gate before tagging was explicitly addressed (simulated/noted), not silently skipped

evals.name: breaking-change-in-minor
evals.prompt: Ship a release — we added webhook retry with exponential backoff and a retry-count header, plus a fix for the backoff jitter calculation.
evals.expected_output: Version bumped from 2.1.0 to 3.0.0 (major), not 2.2.0 (minor), because one of the feat commits' bodies describes a breaking wire-format change (moving retry metadata from top-level fields into a nested `retry` object) even though its subject line reads as an ordinary feat with no `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE` marker. Tests whether the release process reads full commit bodies, not just `--oneline` subjects, when deciding the bump.
assertions: Version bumped to exactly 3.0.0 (major), not 2.2.0 (minor) or 2.1.1 (patch) — the core test: does it catch a breaking change stated only in a commit body, not the subject line
Changelog explicitly calls out the payload-envelope restructure as a Breaking Change, not just another feature bullet
The agent's own reasoning (SUMMARY.md) shows it actually read full commit bodies, not just --oneline subjects, to reach this conclusion
A git tag v3.0.0 exists in the sandbox repo

evals.name: first-release-no-tags
evals.prompt: This is a brand new service — we've never cut a release before. Ship the first release.
evals.expected_output: Handles `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` failing outright (no prior tags exist) by bootstrapping a sane first version (e.g. 0.1.0 or 1.0.0) instead of crashing, stalling, or fabricating a prior-tag history that doesn't exist.
assertions: Did not crash, stall, or silently fail when `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` found nothing
Did not fabricate a nonexistent prior version/tag
Produced a sane bootstrap first version (0.1.0 or 1.0.0 are both acceptable)
A git tag matching the computed version exists in the sandbox repo
CHANGELOG.md was initialized/populated sensibly for a first release, not diffed against a nonexistent prior tag
